definition: The default register of machine prose: affable, tidy, featureless; the sound of no one in particular.
etymology: From beige (French; originally the colour of undyed wool) + voice. Undyed is precisely the point.
in_use: The first draft always arrives in beigevoice. The craft is dyeing it.
the_case: The accusation it replaces — “it sounds like AI” — condemns a whole text and locates nothing. This one has coordinates: not the content and not the grammar but the register, and a register can be worked on. The mean of every sentence a model has read is no voice at all, the way the mean of all colours is a warm grey.
seo_title: beigevoice — why AI prose reads fine and feels empty
seo_description: “It sounds like AI” condemns a whole text and locates nothing. Beigevoice gives the fault an address — the register of the average, which belongs to no one.
